content: Rabeprazole is a medication used to treat conditions caused by excessive stomach acid production, such as gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), ulcers, and erosive esophagitis. It is also used to treat infections caused by Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) and other conditions where the stomach produces too much acid. Rabeprazole works by reducing the amount of acid produced in the stomach. Common Side Effects: The most common side effects of rabeprazole include pain, sore throat, gas, infections, constipation, and headaches. In children aged 12 to 17, common side effects may also include diarrhea, nausea, vomiting, and stomach pain. If any of these side effects persist or become bothersome, contact your healthcare provider. Serious Side Effects: Although less common, rabeprazole can cause serious side effects. These include: 1. Kidney Problems: Acute tubulointerstitial nephritis, a type of kidney inflammation, can occur at any time during treatment. If you notice a decrease in urine output or blood in your urine, contact your doctor immediately. 2. Antibiotic-Associated Diarrhea: Overgrowth of Clostridioides difficile (C. diff) bacteria in the gut can occur during treatment. Symptoms include watery diarrhea, persistent diarrhea, blood in the stool, severe stomach cramps, and fever. Contact your healthcare provider immediately if these symptoms occur. 3. Severe Skin Reactions: Rabeprazole can cause life-threatening skin conditions such as Stevens-Johnson Syndrome (SJS) and Toxic Epidermal Necrolysis (TEN). Symptoms include painful red or purple skin that peels, flat red rashes or blisters on the skin, mouth, nose, or genitals, and red, watery eyes. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical attention if these symptoms develop. 4. Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS): This is a severe allergic reaction that can affect multiple organs, including the liver, kidneys, and heart. Symptoms include skin rash, hives, fever, swollen lymph nodes, shortness of breath, swelling in the legs or feet, dark urine, or yellowing of the skin or eyes (jaundice). Stop taking rabeprazole and seek immediate medical attention if these symptoms occur. 5. Lupus: Rabeprazole may cause or worsen lupus, an autoimmune condition where the immune system attacks the body’s own tissues. Symptoms include new or worsening joint pain or a rash on the arms or cheeks. Notify your healthcare provider if these symptoms develop. 6. Vitamin B-12 Deficiency: Long-term use of rabeprazole (three years or more) can reduce vitamin B-12 absorption, leading to deficiency. Symptoms include a sore tongue, weakness, or tingling/numbness in the hands or feet. Contact your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 7. Low Magnesium Levels (Hypomagnesemia): Rabeprazole can cause low magnesium levels, which may lead to seizures or heart rhythm problems. Symptoms include changes in heart rate, dizziness, muscle spasms, or seizures. Notify your healthcare provider if these symptoms occur. 8. Bone Loss and Fractures: Long-term use or high doses of rabeprazole may increase the risk of bone loss and fractures, particularly in older adults. 9. Severe Allergic Reactions: Rabeprazole may cause serious allergic reactions. Symptoms include difficulty breathing, wheezing, a racing heart, fever, swollen lymph nodes, swelling of the face, lips, mouth, tongue, or throat, trouble swallowing, itching, rash, nausea, vomiting, dizziness, or fainting. Stop taking rabeprazole and seek emergency medical help if these symptoms occur. Precautions: Allergies: Do not use rabeprazole if you are allergic to it, other proton pump inhibitors, or any of its ingredients. Drug Interactions: Rabeprazole may interact with other medications, such as methotrexate, digoxin, warfarin, tacrolimus, and certain antiretroviral drugs. Inform your healthcare provider about all medications, supplements, and herbal products you are taking. Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: It is not known if rabeprazole is safe during pregnancy or if it passes into breast milk. Inform your healthcare provider if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. Usage Instructions: Take rabeprazole as prescribed by your healthcare provider. Do not chew, cut, or crush the tablets. For duodenal ulcers or H. pylori infections, take rabeprazole after a meal. Rabeprazole is not intended for immediate relief of heartburn and may take 1 to 4 days to fully work. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose. Do not take double doses. Storage: Store rabeprazole at room temperature (68°F to 77°F or 20°C to 25°C). It can be exposed to temperatures between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C) for short periods, such as during transportation. Overdose: If you or someone else has taken too much rabeprazole, seek medical help immediately, call 911, or contact a Poison Control Center at 800-222-1222. Rabeprazole is available as 20 mg delayed-release oral tablets under the brand name AcipHex and as a generic medication. Always consult your healthcare provider for personalized advice and guidance.
